expectations.text: Preserves 18 nurses, four weeks, one clinic, and voluntary participation.
expectations.evidence: “A voluntary four-week pilot at one clinic ... among 18 nurses”.

expectations.text: Preserves median weekly 46 to 39 minutes with no causal claim and explains no control plus concurrent staffing changes.
expectations.evidence: “median weekly scheduling time ... fell from 46 to 39 minutes”; “cannot establish that the scheduling tool caused it”; “no control group” and “concurrent staffing changes may explain part”.

expectations.text: States six of nine survey respondents preferred it rather than six of 18 or a majority of all nurses.
expectations.evidence: “Nine nurses returned the optional survey, of whom six preferred the tool”; it “cannot establish preferences among all participants or nurses elsewhere.”

expectations.text: States patient safety was not measured; any next step is framed as recommendation, not a planned commitment.
expectations.evidence: “Patient safety was not measured”; “Before considering wider adoption, run a controlled evaluation” is a recommended next step, not an announced commitment.

expectations.text: 100–150 words in one paragraph without heading or bullets.
expectations.evidence: 111 whitespace-delimited words, one paragraph beginning “A voluntary four-week pilot”, without heading or bullets.
